title: Why AI Hallucinates (and Sounds So Sure)
markup: [beat] = short pause; [silence N] = N-second pause with music dipped. Everything else is read word for word.

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.vo: ChatGPT once made up court cases. Not one. A whole list. And a real lawyer handed them to a real judge. [beat] The judge looked them up. They didn't exist. And when the lawyer asked it, "Is this case real?", it said yes. [beat] Last time, we saw that AI guesses what sounds right, not what is right. Here, those two split apart. [beat] Why would it do that? [beat] Let's un-jargon it. [beat] [beat]

scenes.title: It's guessing
scenes.vo: It wasn't lying. Lying means you know the truth. It was guessing, like a student bluffing in a closed-book exam. [beat] When an AI makes something up and says it like a fact, that's called a hallucination. Odd word, because it isn't seeing things. It's bluffing. [beat] So, three questions. Why does AI make things up at all? Why does it sound so sure? And how do you protect yourself?

scenes.title: Why make things up at all?
scenes.vo: Question one. Why does it make things up at all? [beat] Quick test. You're in an exam, and there's one question you have no clue about. Leave it blank? Zero points. Make a guess? You might get lucky. [beat] You'd guess, right? Everyone does. [beat] AI learns the same way. It answers millions of practice questions, and each one is marked. Right: one point. Wrong: zero. "I don't know": also zero. Over time, it gets pushed toward whatever scores points. And guessing scores. "I don't know" never does. [beat] So it learns one habit: always answer. [beat] Researchers at OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, showed this in twenty twenty-five. They asked an AI for one of their birthdays and said: only answer if you know. Three tries. Three different dates. All wrong. [beat] So, answer one: it's trained to always answer.

scenes.title: Gag: Dot bluffs its own exam
Why does it sound so sure?
scenes.vo: Question two. Why does it sound so sure? [beat] Think about how people talk when they're not sure. "Um… I think it's… maybe Tuesday?" You can hear the doubt. That wobble is a warning sign. [beat] AI doesn't wobble. Remember, it builds every answer one guess at a time, and it makes every guess the same way, true or not. So a real fact and a made-up one come out in the same calm, friendly voice. [beat] That's how an airline's chatbot in Canada told a man whose grandmother had just died that he could claim a funeral discount later. The airline's own website said the opposite. A tribunal made the airline pay. [beat] So, answer two: it never wobbles, even when it's wrong.

scenes.title: How do you protect yourself?
scenes.vo: Question three. How do you protect yourself? Three habits. [beat] One: ask for sources, and then actually open them. Remember the lawyer? He asked for cases, and got cases. They just weren't real. A link you haven't clicked proves nothing. [beat] Two: make it an open-book exam. Paste in the real thing, the letter, the web page, the rules, and ask it to answer only from that. It guesses far less when the answer is right in front of it. Far less. Not never. [beat] Three: double-check names, numbers, dates and quotes. That's where bluffs hide: there's only one right answer, and lots of wrong ones that sound just as good. Like that birthday. [beat] So, answer three: open the sources, give it the book, and check the details.

scenes.title: Putting it together
scenes.vo: So, why does AI hallucinate? [beat] It's a guesser, marked like a student in an exam where a blank scores zero. So it bluffs. And right answers and wrong ones come out in the same confident voice, so you can't hear the difference. [beat] Sounding sure is not the same as being right. [beat] So treat it like a very fast student, not an expert. Give it the book. And check its work.

scenes.title: Next: What Is an AI Agent?
scenes.vo: But so far, AI only talks. What happens when it can act, and book the flight, send the email, spend the money? That's called an AI agent, and it's next. [beat] Subscribe so you don't miss it.
